newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo gold futures fall following IMF news.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo gold futures fall following IMF news.

text.p: Yen-denominated gold futures settled weaker on Friday, after gold dropped overnight after the International Monetary Fund (IMF) said it had majority backing for its gold sale plan, traders said.
"The gold futures market was quiet. Unless uncertainty over the IMF's gold sales plan is removed, investors are unlikely to take new positions," one trader said.
Gold futures ranged from three to five yen per gram lower with benchmark August ending five yen down at 1,339 yen.
Spot gold was quoted at $380.60/90 per ounce at the Tokyo close, against $380.90/381.40 in New York on Thursday.
Traders said mixed trade was detected in the spot gold market, while private investors retreated to the sidelines in the futures market amid sluggish trade.
"In the spot gold market, investment funds are weighing the timing to cover their short positions," the trader said.
Traders said support at $380 per ounce should be solid in the near term, as physical buying interest in Asia could support the market.
In gold futures, massive long positions in the December contract still held by private investors continued to undermine market sentiment, they said.
Other precious metal futures also ended weaker amid bearish sentiment.
In the spot platinum market, selling by overseas investors, absorbing some buying by Japanese trades, pushed down prices.
Spot platinum fell to $385.00/75 per ounce at the Tokyo close after opening at $385.75/386.50.
Benchmark August silver finished 1.3 yen per 10 grams lower at 175.6 yen.
Benchmark August platinum settled seven yen weaker at 1,358 yen.
Benchmark August palladium was down two yen at 422 yen.
